#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
                _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
                return 1
            fi
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Last-resort: try the built-in bash-parallel backend by its known repo path (#1801).
    # This resolves the default even when ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT does not include the
    # installed orch backends (common in integration tests that override ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT).
    # Only bash-parallel gets this treatment — it is the declared system default; any other
    # backend that reaches this point is truly misconfigured.
    local _bash_parallel_sh="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh"
    if [[ "$backend" == "bash-parallel" && -f "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$_bash_parallel_sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
_orch_load_backend() {
    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    local backend

    # Get configured backend; default is bash-parallel (the system default, #1801).
    # "sequential" is no longer a valid backend alias — any unknown alias fails misconfigured.
    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="bash-parallel"
    else
        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-bash-parallel}"
    fi

    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
_orch_load_backend

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
#
# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
fi
# proc-group.sh supplies zbuild_pg_kill for the process-group kill path (#1801).
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/proc-group.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"

# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
    date +%s%N
    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
}

# _orch_local_kill_slot <sig> <wrapper_pid> [inner_pid]
# Kills the wrapper's entire process group (TERM then KILL via zbuild_pg_kill)
# so children that ignore TERM are also terminated (#1801, ADR-011 §kill-path).
# The sig argument is accepted for call-site compatibility but zbuild_pg_kill
# handles its own TERM→KILL escalation internally.
_orch_local_kill_slot() {
    local wrapper_pid="$2"
    local inner_pid="${3:-}"
    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid"
    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" || true
}

# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
#
# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
#
# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local work_unit="$3"
    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"

    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""

    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    local slot_id
    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"

    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
    (
        local rc=0 inner=0
        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
        inner=$!
        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
        trap - EXIT INT TERM
        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
    ) &
    local worker_pid=$!
    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
    echo "$slot_id"
    return 0
}

# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0 timed_out_flag=false
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                timed_out_flag=true
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif $timed_out_flag; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"
        return 1
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"

    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0

    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    sleep 0.5
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    return 0
}

3	# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).

13	# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
16	#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
22	# Collects all results with orch_collect.
23	# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
24	#
25	# Returns:
26	#   0 — all succeeded
27	#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
28	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_fanout() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
37	    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()
38	
39	    local role platform plugin_dir wu
40	    while IFS= read -r role; do
41	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
42	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
43	            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
44	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
46	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
47	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
48	            any_plugin_found=true
49	
50	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
51	                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
52	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
53	                continue
54	            }
55	            work_units+=("$wu")
56	
57	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
58	                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
59	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
60	                continue
61	            }
62	            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
63	            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
64	        done
65	    done <<< "$roles_out"
66	
67	    if ! $any_plugin_found; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial/timed_out named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
            local _fanout_limit; _fanout_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
            warn "fanout: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_fanout_limit}s" || true
            _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
            orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
            _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
            return 1
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
3	# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
4	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
15	# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
16	# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
17	# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
18	_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
19	    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
20	    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
21	        local p
22	        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
23	            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
24	        done
25	        return 0
26	    fi
27	    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
28	    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
29	    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
30	        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
31	        return 1
32	    fi
33	    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
34	    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
35	    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
36	    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
37	    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
38	    local elem
39	    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
40	        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
41	    done
42	}
43	
44	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
45	# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
46	# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
47	# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
48	# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
49	#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
50	#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
51	#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
52	# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
53	# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
54	_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
55	    local raw="${1:-}"
56	    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
57	    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
58	    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
59	    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
60	    local max="$raw"
61	    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
62	    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
63	    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
64	    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
65	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
66	            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
67	        else
68	            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
69	            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
70	        fi
71	    fi
72	    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
73	    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
74	    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
75	    printf '%s' "$max"
76	}
77	
78	# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
79	# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
80	#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
81	#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
82	#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
83	#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
84	#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
85	#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
86	#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
87	#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
88	#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
89	#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
90	#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
91	#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
92	#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
93	#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
94	#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
95	#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
96	#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
97	#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
98	#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
99	#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
100	#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
101	#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
102	#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
103	#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
104	#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
105	#
106	# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
107	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
108	#
109	# Returns:
110	#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
111	#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
112	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
113	#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
114	#   4 — no plugin found for any role
115	#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
116	#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
117	#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
118	#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
119	#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
120	#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
121	# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
122	# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
123	# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
124	_map_unit_element() {
125	    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
126	}
127	
128	# _map_write_summary <stage> <state_file> <env_target> <n> <plugin_dir…> <element…>
129	# #2368: the engine sums up a map group — every element, its outcome and its
130	# one-line reason, read from the element's own primary result — into
131	# artifacts/<stage>-summary.md, and tells later stages whether any element
132	# failed (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED=yes|no). Fail-open: a diagnostic never fails the group.
133	_map_write_summary() {
134	    local stage="$1" state_file="$2" env_target="$3" n="$4"; shift 4
135	    local -a plugins=("${@:1:$n}") elems=("${@:$((n + 1)):$n}")
136	    local state_dir art i raw res line body="" flagged=no outcome reason
137	    state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"; art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$state_dir/artifacts}"
138	    declare -F _registry_output_path_rows >/dev/null 2>&1 \
139	        || source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../../plugin-registry" && pwd)/output-paths.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
140	    for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
141	        raw="$(_registry_output_path_rows "${plugins[$i]}/manifest.yaml" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '$2=="true"{print $1; exit}')"
142	        res=""
143	        if [[ -n "$raw" ]]; then
144	            if [[ -n "$env_target" ]]; then
145	                res="$(export "$env_target=${elems[$i]}"; _registry_resolve_output_path "$raw" "$state_dir" "$art")"
146	            else
147	                _registry_resolve_output_path_v res "$raw" "$state_dir" "$art"
148	            fi
149	        fi
150	        outcome="missing"; reason=""
151	        if [[ -n "$res" && -s "$res" ]]; then
152	            outcome="$(jq -r '.outcome // "missing"' "$res" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
153	            reason="$(jq -r '(.reason // "") | gsub("[\r\n]+"; " ")' "$res" 2>/dev/null || true)"
154	        fi
155	        [[ "$outcome" == fail ]] && flagged=yes
156	        line="- ${elems[$i]}: $outcome${reason:+ — $reason}"
157	        body+="$line"$'\n'
158	    done
159	    export ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED="$flagged"
160	    mkdir -p "$art" 2>/dev/null || true
161	    printf '## %s\n\n%s' "$stage" "$body" > "$art/${stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]/_}-summary.md" 2>/dev/null || true
162	    return 0
163	}
164	
165	_strategy_run_map() {
166	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
167	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
168	    # | infra_failed | failed.
169	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
170	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
171	    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
172	    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
173	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false
174	
175	    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
176	    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
177	    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
178	    local _resolved _res_rc
179	    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
180	    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
181	        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
182	        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
183	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
184	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
185	        return 1
186	    fi
187	
188	    local -a elements=()
189	    local _elem
190	    while IFS= read -r _elem; do
191	        [[ -n "$_elem" ]] && elements+=("$_elem")
192	    done <<< "$_resolved"
193	
194	    if [[ ${#elements[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
195	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
196	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="empty"
197	        return 0
198	    fi
199	
200	    # #1312: resolve the concurrency cap (mirrors ADR-039 FIFO pool).
201	    local max_parallel
202	    max_parallel="$(_strategy_map_resolve_max "$max_raw")"
203	
204	    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): every member runs under <stage>.<element>. Two
205	    # members with one name would write the same records at the same time, so
206	    # the group is refused before any member starts.
207	    # With more than one role every role runs on every element, so the role is
208	    # part of the name: <stage>.<role>.<element>.
209	    local -A _unit_seen=()
210	    local _u_role _u_elem _u_name _u_roles=0
211	    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do [[ -n "$_u_role" ]] && _u_roles=$((_u_roles + 1)); done <<< "$roles_out"
212	    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do
213	        [[ -z "$_u_role" ]] && continue
214	        for _u_elem in "${elements[@]}"; do
215	            _map_unit_element _u_name "$_u_roles" "$_u_role" "$_u_elem"; _u_name="${stage}.${_u_name}"
216	            if [[ -n "${_unit_seen[$_u_name]:-}" ]]; then
217	                warn "map: two members of '$stage' would both run as '$_u_name' — refusing the group" || true
218	                eb_emit_event "strategy.unit_name_conflict" "stage=$stage" "unit=$_u_name" 2>/dev/null || true
219	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
220	                return 1
221	            fi
222	            _unit_seen[$_u_name]=1
223	        done
224	    done <<< "$roles_out"
225	
226	    # Build the ordered list of (plugin_dir, element) work items by iterating
227	    # roles × elements — same order as before, just collected before dispatch.
228	    local -a wu_list=() plugin_list=() elem_list=()
229	    local role element plugin_dir wu
230	    while IFS= read -r role; do
231	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
232	        for element in "${elements[@]}"; do
233	            # Mirror fanout.sh platform-specific then generic resolution.
234	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$element" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
235	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
236	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
237	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
238	            any_plugin_found=true
239	
240	            # Only the platforms dimension populates ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6
241	            # env contract) — pass the element as the 4th arg so the platforms
242	            # path stays byte-identical to fanout. For non-platform dimensions
243	            # (lenses/mutants), pass the generic element identity via args 5+6
244	            # (ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT / ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION, issue #1295, ADR-047 §2)
245	            # so each work unit is distinguishable without hijacking ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
246	            # An optional env_target (arg 7, from the template's `as:`) additionally
247	            # sets a named env var to the element — a generic mapping the strategy
248	            # applies without knowing which dimension or var it is.
249	            _map_unit_element _u_elem "$_u_roles" "$role" "$element"
250	            if [[ "$dimension" == "platforms" ]]; then
251	                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$element" "" "" "" "$_u_elem")"
252	            else
253	                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "generic" "$element" "$dimension" "$env_target" "$_u_elem")"
254	            fi || {
255	                warn "map: failed to create work unit for role=$role element=$element" || true
256	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
257	                continue
258	            }
259	            wu_list+=("$wu")
260	            plugin_list+=("$plugin_dir")
261	            elem_list+=("$element")
262	        done
263	    done <<< "$roles_out"
264	
265	    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
266	        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
267	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
268	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
269	        return 1
270	    fi
271	
272	    # #1312: FIFO-pool batch dispatch — respects max_parallel cap (ADR-039 model).
273	    # Dispatch up to max_parallel work units per batch; collect before advancing.
274	    # This enforces the concurrency cap via the orch backend's own pool machinery.
275	    # Each batch uses a sub-pool so collect drains only the in-flight batch.
276	    # on_member_error=continue: all batches run regardless of prior batch failures.
277	    local total_wu="${#wu_list[@]}"
278	    local batch_start=0 batch_seq=0
279	    local infra_failed=false   # #1312: orch_spawn failure = infra error → fail-closed
280	    local -a batch_plugins=()
281	    # #1312 (Copilot): backends validate pool_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
282	    # The per-batch "-b<N>" suffix must not push the id past 64 chars, or orch_spawn
283	    # fails and the whole batch is silently skipped. Keep the base ≤54 chars so
284	    # "<base>-b<N>" always fits (reserve 10 for the largest realistic suffix, e.g.
285	    # "-b99999999").
286	    #
287	    # #1312 (Copilot): collision-safe truncation. Real pool_ids put their UNIQUE
288	    # tail last ("map-<gid>-$$", "zbuild-<stage>-$$-<ns>"), so a plain prefix
289	    # truncation would drop exactly the disambiguating suffix — two distinct bases
290	    # sharing a 54-char prefix would collide into the same sub-pool dir. Instead,
291	    # when over-long, keep a readable 45-char prefix + an 8-char hash of the FULL
292	    # pool_id (45 + 1 + 8 = 54), so distinct bases yield distinct sub-pool bases.
293	    local _sub_pool_base="$pool_id"
294	    if [[ ${#_sub_pool_base} -gt 54 ]]; then
295	        local _pid_hash
296	        _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
297	        # Fallback if shasum is unavailable: cksum (POSIX) → hex-ish digits.
298	        [[ -n "$_pid_hash" ]] || _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | cksum | cut -c1-8)"
299	        _sub_pool_base="${pool_id:0:45}-${_pid_hash}"
300	    fi
301	    while [[ $batch_start -lt $total_wu ]]; do
302	        batch_seq=$(( batch_seq + 1 ))
303	        local sub_pool_id="${_sub_pool_base}-b${batch_seq}"
304	
305	        # #1312 (Copilot): orch_spawn failure is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, NOT a
306	        # member failure — silently skipping a batch's work units (and possibly
307	        # still returning 0 under on_member_error=continue) hides real breakage.
308	        # Fail closed: stop dispatching and propagate a non-zero rc regardless of
309	        # on_member_error.
310	        if ! orch_spawn "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null; then
311	            warn "map: orch_spawn failed for sub-pool ${sub_pool_id} (infra failure — aborting)" || true
312	            infra_failed=true
313	            break
314	        fi
315	
316	        batch_plugins=()
317	        # #1312 (Copilot): advance batch_start to the next UNPROCESSED index (i),
318	        # NOT by a fixed max_parallel stride. When orch_dispatch fails, batch_dispatched
319	        # does not increment, so the inner loop consumes more than max_parallel indices;
320	        # a fixed stride would then re-process or skip units. `batch_start=i` after the
321	        # loop guarantees every unit is dispatched exactly once.
322	        local batch_dispatched=0 i
323	        for (( i = batch_start; i < total_wu && batch_dispatched < max_parallel; i++ )); do
324	            wu="${wu_list[$i]}"
325	            orch_dispatch "$sub_pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
326	                warn "map: orch_dispatch failed for work unit at index $i" || true
327	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
328	                continue
329	            }
330	            batch_dispatched=$(( batch_dispatched + 1 ))
331	            batch_plugins+=("${plugin_list[$i]}")
332	        done
333	        batch_start=$i
334	
335	        if [[ $batch_dispatched -gt 0 ]]; then
336	            local collect_rc=0
337	            _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
338	            orch_collect "$sub_pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || collect_rc=$?
339	
340	            if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
341	                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
342	                # #1906: artifact enforcement already ran per work unit inside
343	                # plugin_hook_call (scan_plugin_outputs).
344	            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
345	                local _map_limit; _map_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
346	                warn "map: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_map_limit}s" || true
347	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
348	            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
349	                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
350	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
351	            else
352	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
353	            fi
354	        fi
355	
356	        orch_shutdown "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
357	    done
358	
359	    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
360	    _map_write_summary "$stage" "$state_file" "$env_target" "${#plugin_list[@]}" \
361	        "${plugin_list[@]+"${plugin_list[@]}"}" "${elem_list[@]+"${elem_list[@]}"}"
362	    # Shut down the original pool_id (caller spawned it; we use sub-pools per batch
363	    # but the caller's pool must still be closed via orch_shutdown for contract compliance).
364	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
365	
366	    # #1312 (Copilot): infra failure (orch_spawn) fails closed — non-zero rc, NOT
367	    # subject to on_member_error. rc=6 is distinct from member outcomes (0/1/2) so
368	    # the runner surfaces it as a real failure even under on_member_error=continue.
369	    if $infra_failed; then
370	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="infra_failed"
371	        return 1
372	    fi
373	
374	    # #1312: on_member_error=collect (default) — propagate failure outward (group
375	    # fails if any element failed). runner.sh's strategy: map/map:* call sites rely
376	    # on this default. on_member_error=continue mirrors parallel_group_run: all
377	    # elements run regardless of failures; group returns 0 even on partial/all-fail.
378	    #
379	    # #1312 (Copilot): unknown on_member_error values are NOT validated — they fall
380	    # through to the collect branch below (the more CONSERVATIVE default). This
381	    # matches parallel_group_run, which also does not validate: it only special-cases
382	    # its recognised enum (`== "collect"`) and treats anything else as its own safe
383	    # default (parallel-orchestrator.sh:317). Neither path fails loud on a typo. Map
384	    # deliberately picks collect (not continue) as the fall-through so a typo cannot
385	    # accidentally make a group non-blocking — safer to over-report than to swallow
386	    # a failure. (parallel defaults empty→continue; map defaults empty→collect per
387	    # its strategy: call-site contract, but both fall through to their safe default.)
388	    if [[ "$on_member_error" == "continue" ]]; then
389	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
390	        return 0
391	    fi
392	
393	    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
394	    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
395	    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
396	    fi
397	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
        local p
        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
    local elem
    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
    done
}

# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
    local raw="${1:-}"
    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
    local max="$raw"
    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
        else
            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
        fi
    fi
    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
    printf '%s' "$max"
}

# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
#   4 — no plugin found for any role
#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
_map_unit_element() {
    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
}

# _map_write_summary <stage> <state_file> <env_target> <n> <plugin_dir…> <element…>
# #2368: the engine sums up a map group — every element, its outcome and its
# one-line reason, read from the element's own primary result — into
# artifacts/<stage>-summary.md, and tells later stages whether any element
# failed (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED=yes|no). Fail-open: a diagnostic never fails the group.
_map_write_summary() {
    local stage="$1" state_file="$2" env_target="$3" n="$4"; shift 4
    local -a plugins=("${@:1:$n}") elems=("${@:$((n + 1)):$n}")
    local state_dir art i raw res line body="" flagged=no outcome reason
    state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"; art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$state_dir/artifacts}"
    declare -F _registry_output_path_rows >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        || source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../../plugin-registry" && pwd)/output-paths.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
    for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
        raw="$(_registry_output_path_rows "${plugins[$i]}/manifest.yaml" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '$2=="true"{print $1; exit}')"
        res=""
        if [[ -n "$raw" ]]; then
            if [[ -n "$env_target" ]]; then
                res="$(export "$env_target=${elems[$i]}"; _registry_resolve_output_path "$raw" "$state_dir" "$art")"
            else
                _registry_resolve_output_path_v res "$raw" "$state_dir" "$art"
            fi
        fi
        outcome="missing"; reason=""
        if [[ -n "$res" && -s "$res" ]]; then
            outcome="$(jq -r '.outcome // "missing"' "$res" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
            reason="$(jq -r '(.reason // "") | gsub("[\r\n]+"; " ")' "$res" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        fi
        [[ "$outcome" == fail ]] && flagged=yes
        line="- ${elems[$i]}: $outcome${reason:+ — $reason}"
        body+="$line"$'\n'
    done
    export ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED="$flagged"
    mkdir -p "$art" 2>/dev/null || true
    printf '## %s\n\n%s' "$stage" "$body" > "$art/${stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]/_}-summary.md" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

_strategy_run_map() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false

    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
    local _resolved _res_rc
    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
        return 1
    fi

    local -a elements=()
    local _elem
    while IFS= read -r _elem; do
        [[ -n "$_elem" ]] && elements+=("$_elem")
    done <<< "$_resolved"

    if [[ ${#elements[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="empty"
        return 0
    fi

    # #1312: resolve the concurrency cap (mirrors ADR-039 FIFO pool).
    local max_parallel
    max_parallel="$(_strategy_map_resolve_max "$max_raw")"

    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): every member runs under <stage>.<element>. Two
    # members with one name would write the same records at the same time, so
    # the group is refused before any member starts.
    # With more than one role every role runs on every element, so the role is
    # part of the name: <stage>.<role>.<element>.
    local -A _unit_seen=()
    local _u_role _u_elem _u_name _u_roles=0
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do [[ -n "$_u_role" ]] && _u_roles=$((_u_roles + 1)); done <<< "$roles_out"
    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do
        [[ -z "$_u_role" ]] && continue
        for _u_elem in "${elements[@]}"; do
            _map_unit_element _u_name "$_u_roles" "$_u_role" "$_u_elem"; _u_name="${stage}.${_u_name}"
            if [[ -n "${_unit_seen[$_u_name]:-}" ]]; then
                warn "map: two members of '$stage' would both run as '$_u_name' — refusing the group" || true
                eb_emit_event "strategy.unit_name_conflict" "stage=$stage" "unit=$_u_name" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            fi
            _unit_seen[$_u_name]=1
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    # Build the ordered list of (plugin_dir, element) work items by iterating
    # roles × elements — same order as before, just collected before dispatch.
    local -a wu_list=() plugin_list=() elem_list=()
    local role element plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for element in "${elements[@]}"; do
            # Mirror fanout.sh platform-specific then generic resolution.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$element" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            # Only the platforms dimension populates ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6
            # env contract) — pass the element as the 4th arg so the platforms
            # path stays byte-identical to fanout. For non-platform dimensions
            # (lenses/mutants), pass the generic element identity via args 5+6
            # (ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT / ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION, issue #1295, ADR-047 §2)
            # so each work unit is distinguishable without hijacking ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
            # An optional env_target (arg 7, from the template's `as:`) additionally
            # sets a named env var to the element — a generic mapping the strategy
            # applies without knowing which dimension or var it is.
            _map_unit_element _u_elem "$_u_roles" "$role" "$element"
            if [[ "$dimension" == "platforms" ]]; then
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$element" "" "" "" "$_u_elem")"
            else
                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "generic" "$element" "$dimension" "$env_target" "$_u_elem")"
            fi || {
                warn "map: failed to create work unit for role=$role element=$element" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            wu_list+=("$wu")
            plugin_list+=("$plugin_dir")
            elem_list+=("$element")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: FIFO-pool batch dispatch — respects max_parallel cap (ADR-039 model).
    # Dispatch up to max_parallel work units per batch; collect before advancing.
    # This enforces the concurrency cap via the orch backend's own pool machinery.
    # Each batch uses a sub-pool so collect drains only the in-flight batch.
    # on_member_error=continue: all batches run regardless of prior batch failures.
    local total_wu="${#wu_list[@]}"
    local batch_start=0 batch_seq=0
    local infra_failed=false   # #1312: orch_spawn failure = infra error → fail-closed
    local -a batch_plugins=()
    # #1312 (Copilot): backends validate pool_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
    # The per-batch "-b<N>" suffix must not push the id past 64 chars, or orch_spawn
    # fails and the whole batch is silently skipped. Keep the base ≤54 chars so
    # "<base>-b<N>" always fits (reserve 10 for the largest realistic suffix, e.g.
    # "-b99999999").
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): collision-safe truncation. Real pool_ids put their UNIQUE
    # tail last ("map-<gid>-$$", "zbuild-<stage>-$$-<ns>"), so a plain prefix
    # truncation would drop exactly the disambiguating suffix — two distinct bases
    # sharing a 54-char prefix would collide into the same sub-pool dir. Instead,
    # when over-long, keep a readable 45-char prefix + an 8-char hash of the FULL
    # pool_id (45 + 1 + 8 = 54), so distinct bases yield distinct sub-pool bases.
    local _sub_pool_base="$pool_id"
    if [[ ${#_sub_pool_base} -gt 54 ]]; then
        local _pid_hash
        _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
        # Fallback if shasum is unavailable: cksum (POSIX) → hex-ish digits.
        [[ -n "$_pid_hash" ]] || _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | cksum | cut -c1-8)"
        _sub_pool_base="${pool_id:0:45}-${_pid_hash}"
    fi
    while [[ $batch_start -lt $total_wu ]]; do
        batch_seq=$(( batch_seq + 1 ))
        local sub_pool_id="${_sub_pool_base}-b${batch_seq}"

        # #1312 (Copilot): orch_spawn failure is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, NOT a
        # member failure — silently skipping a batch's work units (and possibly
        # still returning 0 under on_member_error=continue) hides real breakage.
        # Fail closed: stop dispatching and propagate a non-zero rc regardless of
        # on_member_error.
        if ! orch_spawn "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null; then
            warn "map: orch_spawn failed for sub-pool ${sub_pool_id} (infra failure — aborting)" || true
            infra_failed=true
            break
        fi

        batch_plugins=()
        # #1312 (Copilot): advance batch_start to the next UNPROCESSED index (i),
        # NOT by a fixed max_parallel stride. When orch_dispatch fails, batch_dispatched
        # does not increment, so the inner loop consumes more than max_parallel indices;
        # a fixed stride would then re-process or skip units. `batch_start=i` after the
        # loop guarantees every unit is dispatched exactly once.
        local batch_dispatched=0 i
        for (( i = batch_start; i < total_wu && batch_dispatched < max_parallel; i++ )); do
            wu="${wu_list[$i]}"
            orch_dispatch "$sub_pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "map: orch_dispatch failed for work unit at index $i" || true
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
                continue
            }
            batch_dispatched=$(( batch_dispatched + 1 ))
            batch_plugins+=("${plugin_list[$i]}")
        done
        batch_start=$i

        if [[ $batch_dispatched -gt 0 ]]; then
            local collect_rc=0
            _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
            orch_collect "$sub_pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || collect_rc=$?

            if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                # #1906: artifact enforcement already ran per work unit inside
                # plugin_hook_call (scan_plugin_outputs).
            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
                local _map_limit; _map_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
                warn "map: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_map_limit}s" || true
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            else
                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
            fi
        fi

        orch_shutdown "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    done

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
    _map_write_summary "$stage" "$state_file" "$env_target" "${#plugin_list[@]}" \
        "${plugin_list[@]+"${plugin_list[@]}"}" "${elem_list[@]+"${elem_list[@]}"}"
    # Shut down the original pool_id (caller spawned it; we use sub-pools per batch
    # but the caller's pool must still be closed via orch_shutdown for contract compliance).
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    # #1312 (Copilot): infra failure (orch_spawn) fails closed — non-zero rc, NOT
    # subject to on_member_error. rc=6 is distinct from member outcomes (0/1/2) so
    # the runner surfaces it as a real failure even under on_member_error=continue.
    if $infra_failed; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="infra_failed"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1312: on_member_error=collect (default) — propagate failure outward (group
    # fails if any element failed). runner.sh's strategy: map/map:* call sites rely
    # on this default. on_member_error=continue mirrors parallel_group_run: all
    # elements run regardless of failures; group returns 0 even on partial/all-fail.
    #
    # #1312 (Copilot): unknown on_member_error values are NOT validated — they fall
    # through to the collect branch below (the more CONSERVATIVE default). This
    # matches parallel_group_run, which also does not validate: it only special-cases
    # its recognised enum (`== "collect"`) and treats anything else as its own safe
    # default (parallel-orchestrator.sh:317). Neither path fails loud on a typo. Map
    # deliberately picks collect (not continue) as the fall-through so a typo cannot
    # accidentally make a group non-blocking — safer to over-report than to swallow
    # a failure. (parallel defaults empty→continue; map defaults empty→collect per
    # its strategy: call-site contract, but both fall through to their safe default.)
    if [[ "$on_member_error" == "continue" ]]; then
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
        return 0
    fi

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
#   stage      — stage name
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_sequential() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local any_plugin_found=false

    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            prc=0
            orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || prc=$?
            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true

            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
                if [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
                    local _seq_limit; _seq_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
                    warn "sequential: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_seq_limit}s" || true
                    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
                else
                    warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
                    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                fi
                return 1
            fi

        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
    return 0
}
